name: mcp-bridge-vscode
description: Let an MCP client (such as Claude Desktop) work in VS Code: files, a visible terminal, git, diagnostics and more, with approvals for risky actions.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Tools stay disabled in Restricted Mode unless mcpBridge.allowInUntrustedWorkspace is enabled (user settings only).

commands.title: MCP Bridge: Connect to Claude Desktop
MCP Bridge: Disconnect from Claude Desktop
MCP Bridge: Pause / Resume AI Access

enumDescriptions: Risky actions need approval in chat; the highest-risk ones also need a VS Code confirmation box (recommended).
Approval in chat only. Faster, but the server cannot verify a human clicked.

mcpBridge.allowedRoots.description: Extra folders where file writes need no approval (workspace folders are always allowed).

mcpBridge.allowInUntrustedWorkspace.description: Let tools run even in Restricted Mode. Risky; off by default.

mcpBridge.redactSecrets.description: Mask API keys, tokens and private keys in tool output before it is sent to the AI.

mcpBridge.protectedPaths.description: Extra paths or patterns (* wildcard) that need approval to read or change, in addition to the built-in credential locations (.ssh, .aws, .env files, keys and similar).

mcpBridge.extraInstructions.description: Your own rules for the AI, one per line (for example: Always ask before git push). They are added to the bridge's instructions. They cannot switch off approvals or protections, which the extension enforces itself. Takes effect the next time Claude Desktop connects (restart it).

enumDescriptions: Run the bridge shim with VS Code's own runtime. No Node.js install needed (recommended).
Run the shim with the node program found on PATH.
mcpBridge.shimRuntime.description: Which runtime Claude Desktop uses to start the bridge shim. Applies the next time you run MCP Bridge: Connect to Claude Desktop.

mcpBridge.maxTerminals.description: Maximum terminals the bridge keeps open.

mcpBridge.idleMinutes.description: Close bridge terminals idle for this many minutes.
